extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers of invertebrate zoology and bryozoan taxonomy
extracted.subtask_description: Morphological, developmental, reproductive, and ecological criteria for identifying, classifying, and describing freshwater Polyzoa (Bryozoa/Entoprocta) including orders, suborders, genera, and diagnostic structures such as statoblasts, lips, collars, and epistomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anus position: Entoprocta vs Ectoprocta
rubrics_metrics.description: Entoprocta: the anus as well as the mouth is enclosed in the circle of tentacles; Ectoprocta: the anus is outside the circle of tentacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the relative position of the anus to the tentacular crown as a primary diagnostic character distinguishing the two subclasses; note also that in Entoprocta the zooecium is not very distinctly separated from the polypide, whereas in Ectoprocta it is distinguishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colony formation: solitary vs permanent colonial
rubrics_metrics.description: Some entoprocts are solitary or form temporary colonies by budding; ectoprocts form permanent communities by budding with individuals remaining connected by living tissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe whether individuals remain permanently connected (ectoproctous colonies) or are solitary/temporary aggregates (some entoprocts) to inform classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence/absence of epistome (Gymnolæmata vs Phylactolæmata)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gymnolæmata (Order I): polypides have no epistome; Phylactolæmata (Order II): polypides have a leaf-shaped epistome projecting upwards and forwards between the mouth and anus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of an epistome is an essential distinguishing character separating Phylactolæmata (freshwater) from Gymnolæmata; examine the tentacular crown region for a projecting epistome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of zooecia (Gymnolæmata character)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Gymnolæmata the zooecia are in nearly all cases distinctly separated from one another by transverse perforated plates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for transverse perforated partitions between zooecia when diagnosing Gymnolæmata; absence or indistinct separation indicates other groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cheilostomata: lip/lid (suborder diagnostic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cheilostomata zooecia are provided with a 'lip' or lid hinged to the posterior margin of the orifice; the lid closes automatically and is pushed open by expanding tentacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for a hinged opercular lip/peristome and flattened zooecia; presence of modified zooecia (avicularia, vibracula) supports Cheilostomata placement; note ecological tendency (mainly marine, some brackish).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ctenostomata: collar-like membrane (suborder diagnostic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ctenostomata zooecia possess a collar-like membrane pleated vertically that closes above the polypide when retracted and is thrust out and expanded into a ring just prior to tentacle extrusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnostic character: a pleated collar/extrusible ring. Zooecia often tubular (sometimes flattened); many marine but some sections inhabit fresh water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclostomata: neither lip nor collar (suborder diagnostic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyclostomata zooecia are provided neither with a lip nor with a collar-like membrane; they are tubular and usually have circular orifices; the group is exclusively marine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of both opercular lip and collar, combined with tubular zooecia and circular orifice, indicates Cyclostomata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phylactolæmata diagnostic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Polypides possess a leaf-shaped epistome between mouth and anus; zooecia are not distinct from one another, and zoaria may be divided by chitinous partitions in dendritic forms; Phylactolæmata are exclusively freshwater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combination of epistome presence, indistinct zooecia, and freshwater habitat to place specimens in Phylactolæmata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblast structure and classification importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Statoblasts are internal buds arising from the funiculus, composed of cells with abundant food-material and enclosed in a capsule with thick horny walls; often surrounded by a swim-ring of horny-walled chambers filled with air; external form of statoblasts is very important in the classification of the Phylactolæmata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine statoblast shape (flattened, oval, circular), presence/absence and form of swim-ring and marginal processes; these external characters are key diagnostic features for phylactolæmatous genera and species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resting buds (Paludicellidæ) as diagnostic and ecological features
rubrics_metrics.description: Paludicellidæ produce external resting buds resembling statoblasts—masses of cells with food-material, protected by a thick horny coat—produced at the points ordinary buds would form; these are seasonal and may be produced in winter in Europe and at hot-weather onset in India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition of external resting buds and their seasonal timing can distinguish Paludicellidæ and inform ecological/biogeographic identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budding pattern in freshwater ctenostomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically three buds are produced from each zooecium—one anterior and two lateral opposite one another—so that, with the parent zooecium behind, each zooecium (except at ends) connects with four others forming a cross; lateral buds may be suppressed producing linear series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the arrangement and timing of daughter and granddaughter buds (cross vs linear, suppression of laterals) as diagnostic for freshwater ctenostome genera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budding pattern in Phylactolæmata
rubrics_metrics.description: Linear budding is typical, but granddaughter-buds are produced long before daughter-buds are mature, causing zooecia to be pressed together and lateral buds to appear irregularly; adventitious buds may occur near zooecial tips (e.g., Victorella).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing relationships of bud generations and degree of crowding/irregular lateral buds help distinguish phylactolæmatous growth forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Polyzoa reproduce by (i) eggs, (ii) budding, and (iii) asexual dormant bodies (statoblasts/resting buds); most species are hermaphrodite with reproductive organs on the inner surface of the endocyst often in definite positions connected with the funiculus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record whether reproduction observed is sexual (eggs/larvae) or asexual (budding, statoblasts), and note hermaphroditic condition and location of gonads relative to funiculus for species descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embryonic development from the egg
rubrics_metrics.description: Egg enclosed in membrane forms hollow sphere by regular division, becomes ovoid and ciliated, breaks into zooecial cavity; inside, polypide(s) form by a budding-like process; larva becomes pear-shaped, exits via a degenerate bud/orifice, swims briefly, attaches by broad end, everts polypide, and develops zoarium by budding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use larval morphology (ciliated pear-shaped larva, internal budding of polypide), exit route, and attachment/inversion behavior as developmental characters in life-history-based diagnoses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development from statoblasts and resting buds
rubrics_metrics.description: Statoblast capsule often splits longitudinally into two valves through which the young polypide emerges, adheres, and produces a new zoarium by budding; variations exist (e.g., Victorella where a projection forms tip of new zooecium); statoblasts can remain dormant for months/years and germination cues vary geographically (cold in Europe, rains/temperature changes in India).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document capsule opening mode, valve retention, and environmental cues for germination when using statoblast development as a taxonomic or ecological trait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Movement of zoarium vs polypide
rubrics_metrics.description: In most polyzoa movement is confined to the polypide; in a few freshwater genera (Cristatella, Lophopus, Lophopodella, Pectinatella) the whole zoarium can progress using a specialized mucus-covered 'sole' or by alternate expansion/contraction of the base or lifting the anterior base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe whether movement involves only polypide extrusion/retraction or whole-zoarium locomotion; presence of a sole or specialized base strongly implicates genera capable of zoarium progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanics of lophophore extrusion and retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction is effected by retractor muscles pulling extruded parts back; extrusion may be assisted by relaxation of retractor and parieto-vaginal muscles and action of parietal muscles, hydrostatic forces, or resilience of inverted ectocyst; in some taxa protrusion can occur even after zooecium is cut open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing musculature and functional morphology, examine retractor, parietal, and parieto-vaginal muscles and consider hydrostatic/extracystic contributions to protrusion/extrusion in functional descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tentacle and feeding behavior as diagnostic observations
rubrics_metrics.description: When expanded tentacles remain mostly still aside from ciliary motion, but individual tentacles can be bent to wave away unsuitable particles; ciliary currents bring food and non-food particles elicit local tentacular movements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record tentacle responsiveness and ciliary feeding behavior in behavioral descriptions; specific responses may aid ecological interpretation though they are not strictly taxonomic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized zooecia with movement (avicularia and vibracula)
rubrics_metrics.description: In cheilostomes certain individuals (avicularia and vibracula) are morphologically modified and show almost constant rhythmical or convulsive movements: avicularia shaped like a bird's beak that snap, vibracula are thread-like and wave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence, form, and behavior of specialized zooecia (avicularia, vibracula) are important characters for species/genus identification within Cheilostomata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblast external form and geographic/seasonal distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: External form of statoblasts (flattened, oval, circular) is important in classification of phylactolæmata; production timing varies by climate (e.g., many temperate species produce statoblasts before winter; in India many species produce more at the onset of hot weather or rains).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statoblast morphology combined with phenology (season of production) as diagnostic and biogeographic evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brown bodies and polypide coloration
rubrics_metrics.description: Brown bodies are formed by degeneration of a polypide as preparation for regeneration and their pigment is the main colouring matter in polypides; young polypides are generally colourless; brown bodies may be conspicuous in some genera (Hislopia, Victorella) and can extrude the collar-like membrane in ctenostomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note presence/visibility of brown bodies and pigmentation states in specimens, as these structures can be taxonomically and developmentally informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic distribution as supporting taxonomic evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of genera (which genera occur in India, which are widespread or restricted) is summarized: e.g., Victorella occurs in Europe, India, Africa, Australia; Plumatella occurs in all geographical regions; some genera are regionally restricted (Australella N.S. Wales, Stephanella Japan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use documented geographic ranges as corroborative evidence in identifications, but corroborate morphological characters since ranges may overlap or be incompletely known.
